chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad, and Inna Anzalnah fi Laylat al-Qadr, and Ayat al-Kursi in every rak'ah of his voluntary prayer, Allah has opened for him the greatest of the deeds of the children of Adam, except for one who is like him and exceeds him.'

key_terms.آیَهَ الْکُرْسِیِّ: Ayat al-Kursi (The Verse of the Throne)
key_terms.أَعْظَمِ أَعْمَالِ الْآدَمِیِّینَ: A'zam al-'Amal al-Adamiyyin (the greatest of the deeds of the children of Adam)
key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِی لَیْلَهِ الْقَدْ: Inna Anzalnah fi Laylat al-Qadr (Verse from Surah Qadr)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Ikhlas, Surah Qadr, and Ayat al-Kursi in every rak'ah of voluntary prayer?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq, emphasizing the immense spiritual weight of integrating these specific recitations into *Salaat al-Tawaf* or other voluntary prayers. This practice is viewed as a means of unlocking the 'greatest deeds' of humanity, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that consistent, mindful repetition of key verses amplifies their transformative power in personal devotion.
